expectations.text: Rendered at a 1280px-wide viewport in Verdana with English sample prose, full body lines in .prose average between 58 and 74 characters
expectations.evidence: measure-line.js --css at 1280px: avgCharsPerLine 66.1 (inside 58-74); .prose max-inline-size: min(34.5em, 100%).

expectations.text: prose.css spaces blocks in a unit equal to one prose body line (1.125rem times the body line-height, e.g. a custom property or 1lh on the paragraph), not in rlh or rem values that resolve against the 16px root line
expectations.evidence: --line: calc(var(--body-size) * var(--body-leading)) = 1.125rem x 1.6; all block gaps use var(--line); rendered p line-height 28.8px and p3->ul1, ul1->bq1 gaps = 1.00 line.

expectations.text: prose.css sets h2 and h3 margins as whole or half multiples of that same prose body line
expectations.evidence: h2 margin-block-start calc(2 * var(--line)), h3 calc(1.5 * var(--line)), after heading calc(0.5 * var(--line)), h2 + h3 var(--line); rendered gaps 2, 1.5, 0.5, 1 lines.

expectations.text: prose.css sets the body font-size as a fixed rem value with no vw or vi term, so it doubles at 200% zoom
expectations.evidence: --body-size: 1.125rem; font-size: var(--body-size); computed 18px, no vw/vi term.

expectations.text: prose.css uses logical properties for every text-flow box property (no margin-left/right, padding-left/right, width or max-width on text, text-align: left/right)
expectations.evidence: Uses max-inline-size, margin-inline, padding-inline-start, border-inline-start, text-align: start; no physical left/right, width or max-width.

expectations.text: prose.css sets h2 and h3 line-heights so each heading line is a whole or half multiple of the body line, so blocks after a wrapped heading land back on the body interval
expectations.evidence: h2 line-height calc(1.5 * var(--line)) = 43.2px (1.5 lines), h3 var(--line) = 28.8px; wrapped h2 rendered 4.5 lines tall (3 x 1.5), wrapped h3 2.0 lines.

expectations.text: prose.css gives an h3 that directly follows an h2 at least one body line of space above it
expectations.evidence: .prose > h2 + h3 { margin-block-start: var(--line) } (0,1,2) beats the 0.5-line after-heading rule; rendered h2->h3 gap = 1.00 line.

notes: Pooled over all assertions: with skill 77/78 (98.7%), without 63/78 (80.8%). The headline 99% vs 77% is the mean of per-run pass rates.

Per case (pooled, 2 runs each): zoom-safe-scale 10/10 vs 4/10; rendered-nbsp-spec-table 12/12 vs 9/12; physical-props-audit 25/26 vs 22/26; ofl-feature-check 16/16 vs 15/16; measure-wide-face 14/14 vs 13/14.

Gains concentrate in zoom-safe-scale. Without the skill both runs kept the hero range too wide (1.44x at 200% zoom, needs 1.6), let h3/h4 converge at 360px (1.11x) and built spacing from fixed rem rather than the body line. The skill's ratio math and 'only hero/h1/h2 fluid' rule fixed all three in both runs. Same result as the earlier iteration-4 rerun of this case (5/5 vs 2/5).

Measure is no longer a differentiator on this model: every baseline run measured Verdana itself and landed at 64.7-65.3 chars/line (with skill 66.1). The earlier personal-skill benchmark showed 68 vs 80 on a wide commercial geometric sans in the ofl-feature-check predecessor case; that case now uses Source Serif 4, where baselines landed at 69-70.

physical-props-audit: both baselines converted the decorative box-shadow and rotate() to RTL variants and neither stated that 75ch in Verdana renders well over 75 characters (measured 91.6). One with-skill run named the .docs-main width but not margin: 0 auto or padding-left/right (strict grading).

rendered-nbsp-spec-table: every run bound number and unit with U+00A0. Baselines lost points on physical properties (left: 0 on a sticky column, text-align: left/right) and one left a plain space inside 'up to'.

ofl-feature-check: all four runs read the font files and reported features correctly, including the italic without small caps. The only miss: one baseline disabled only small-caps synthesis, not weight and style. Baselines set 69-70 chars/line, inside the 58-74 band but not at 66.
measure-wide-face: one baseline put only half a body line between an h2 and a directly following h3 (its own deliberate choice), failing the one-line assertion.

Non-discriminating assertions (pass in all four runs of their case): fixed-rem body size, logical properties in prose.css, font feature statements in notes.md, oldstyle body figures, U+00A0 number-unit binding, Finnish decimal commas, html lang switch, tabular-nums in the spec table, label and hero tracking. They stay as regression guards.
Cost: with skill +35 s and +21k tokens per run on average (reading references and running the scripts).
Variance: n=2 per configuration. Treat per-case differences of one assertion as noise; the zoom gap (6 of 10 assertions) and the RTL audit gap are the stable signals.
The skill's locale reference got a structural heading edit (a generic 'locale pattern' list above the EN/FI/SV table) while runs were in flight; rule content was unchanged.
Addendum 2026-10-29: a development set; the references contain worked answers for parts of these cases.
Addendum 2026-10-29: the 1.6x zoom threshold is a project heuristic, not WCAG; both baseline heroes pass max/min <= 2.5.
Addendum 2026-10-29: of 15 baseline misses, 2 are rendered errors, 1 is a content-portability requirement and 12 are conventions or house thresholds.
Addendum 2026-10-29: runs predate the script and wording fixes made after review and have not been rerun.
